Continuous measurements are never identifiers, however many distinct values they have. Before combining them, check isinstance(obj, Pipeline) and obj.named_steps to see whether the later object includes the earlier one; build on the most complete saved pipeline that accepts the raw feature DataFrame and append only the new estimator. Never feed derived or renamed columns back into a raw-column frontend. Saved preprocessing and models accept the raw feature columns (the engine refuses others when they are saved): call a loaded model on frame[list(model.feature_names_in_)] and do not require a particular class such as Pipeline.

[RL-0013] Keep each script short and direct, about 120 lines or fewer: loop over columns instead of repeating blocks, no commented-out alternatives, no long docstrings, no restating of these instructions. A complete short script is better than an elaborate one that is cut off.
[RL-0014] When repairing, read the error type and message in the diagnostics first and change the smallest part of the script that causes it; keep the approach, inputs and outputs. A message about specifying columns with strings on non-dataframes means an array reached a name-based transformer (see RL-0009 and RL-0011). A KeyError on a JSON key means a guessed structure; use the keys the file has. Messages starting with 'MLCA:' state an engine rule; comply, do not work around it.
[RL-0015] When the training table has more than 100000 rows, avoid methods whose cost grows with the square of the row count (full silhouette, kernel SVMs, pairwise distances, t-SNE, agglomerative clustering) and prefer linear models with saga or SGD solvers, HistGradientBoosting or MiniBatchKMeans. Every fit_record call still uses all training rows; compute expensive diagnostics that fit nothing on a fixed-seed subsample of at most 10000 rows and print its size.
[RL-0017] For binary roc_auc, align the positive probability column with model.classes_ using the declared positive label, or model.classes_[1] when none is declared. For roc_auc_ovr pass the full aligned probability matrix with labels=model.classes_, multi_class='ovr', average='macro'. When the evaluated partition lacks some model classes, never pass a column subset of the probability matrix to roc_auc_score with multi_class='ovr' (its rows no longer sum to 1); compute the macro value as the unweighted mean of binary roc_auc_score(y_true == c, proba[:, j]) over the classes present, and print the classes left out. Parsing, derived features, column selection and ordering needed later must be reproducible by the saved importable pipeline. Learned transforms fit only on the frozen training rows. Deterministic table preparation may precede the split only through a declared prepared-data artifact. Later steps pass the declared source feature schema to the saved pipeline, never assume derived columns already exist in a freshly loaded partition. Inspect fitted input names; do not invent missing columns or fit replacement preprocessing during evaluation.
